recipes.name: Farmer's Market Vegetarian Quesadillas
ingredients_raw: 1.25 cups shredded reduced-fat sharp Cheddar cheese

steps.text: Cook red pepper, zucchini, yellow squash, onion, and mushrooms in olive oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium to medium-high heat until just tender, about 7 minutes. Transfer vegetables to a bowl.

Coat same skillet with cooking spray; place one tortilla in skillet. Sprinkle 1/4 cup cheese evenly over tortilla; layer 3/4 cup vegetable mixture on top. Sprinkle 1/8 cup more cheese on vegetables; top with a second tortilla. Cook until golden on both sides, about 2 to 3 minutes per side. Transfer quesadilla to a cutting board; cut into 8 triangles with a pizza cutter. Repeat with remaining ingredients. Serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Farmer's Market Vegetarian Quesadillas
raw_recipe.description: Making the most of simple, fresh ingredients found at your local Farmer's Market, these quesadillas make great appetizers or a quick and healthy meal.

review.reviewBody: These were good. I added some garlic powder and salt and pepper when sauteing. And some chopped fresh basil too. I baked them in the oven instead of doing them in the skillet. I just brushed some olive oil on the tortillas, turned them oil side down on a baking sheet and put some filling and cheese on one side and folded over, then stuck them in a 425 degree oven for about 5 minutes to get a little crunch out of the tortillas. Thanks for a great idea!

I submitted this recipe, and you can use any vegetable you like--adding eggplant, spinach, or black beans also works well. Have fun using the fresh ingredients your family enjoys! This recipe makes 6 servings out of the 3 quesadillas. You can use reduced carb tortillas also, and more cheese, but this was created to be a healthy recipe ; ).

*** WORTHY OF TEN STARS ** These quesadillas were fantastic!! I also followed Nugget's suggestion of filling 1/2 of a large tortilla, folding over, and baking in the oven at 425 degrees for about 8-10 minutes or until brown. I also added some garlic powder and onion powder to the veggies while they were cooking. You can top the quesadillas with sour cream, salsa, and sliced avocado too. So healthy, so delicious! Excellent recipe!

Great base recipe. I am not a fan of squash or zucchini so made mine with cheddar, mushrooms, onion and spinach. These are great with the whole wheat tortillas and especially yummy with the spinach and herb tortillas!! :)

These are SO! GOOD! Even carnivores can’t resist! The mixed tastes and textures: mushrooms, zucchini, red onions and more! Oh my! Hearty and filling! I was sure to include all veggies as stated but added a chopped jalapeño. I did everything on my Blackstone - seasoning with a little S&P and garlic powder. Used 4 cheese Mexican Blend. While I think this is delicious as written, I could see LIGHTLY seasoning the veggies with some cumin or taco seasoning. If you do take this recommend - be light handed as you want the flavor of these amazing vegetables to shine through. And - as I said, great as is! Thanks Jennifer! Will make again!

These were sooo good! I used the veggies I had (as suggested). So, mine consisted of red and green bell peppers, spinach, mushrooms, shallots, and corn. I also used colby because that's a preference and whole wheat carb balance burritos. I toasted one side in the pan them flipped them and filled the toasted side with the veggies and cheese while the other side toasted. I don't like soggy tortillas and thought this would help prevent that. It worked perfectly! These were really filling and incredible without seasoning! I will definitely be making these again!

Simple. Delicious. Healthy. I followed suggestions from a couple of the reviews, adding seasoning (I used McCormick’s Garlic ‘n Herb and a pinch of salt) and baking the quesadillas in a 425 degree oven for 8-9 minutes. I will definitely make this again!

I chopped, then placed the veggies in 1 Tbsp of grapeseed oil in a plastic zip bag adding seasoning salt & pepper. After thoroughly coating the veggies with oil and seasonings in the bag, I poured the oiled veggies into a grilling basket and roasted then on the patio grill. Remove the veggies when cooked and assemble the quesadillas. Spread a little oil on the both sides of the outside of the tortilla of the assembled quesadillas and finish grilling on the hot grill. Now, that's a great summer meal.

Recipe #1 of our new vegetarian/vegan lifestyle! I added fresh basil, sea salt, black pepper, green bell pepper, fresh minced garlic, and onion powder. I have a quesadilla maker which made for easy cooking. Used my food chopper but next time I would slice the veggies instead so that the quesadillas are thicker.
I sauteed garlic with sesame oil, then added green, yellow, red peppers, mushrooms, onions, pepper and salt and wow it was amazing! I also used coconut Pam spray for the tortillas..

This was great! I liked sautéing the veggies first then adding them to the quesadilla. Being I was making 8, I used a sheet pan lined with parchment paper and baked them all at once at 350 for 6-8 minutes. Served them with rice, corn, avocado and fresh salsa.

I followed the recipe pretty closely except for using closer to 1 cup of each of the veggies. It was good with just salt and pepper, but different spices could definitely be added. I was actually surprised at how much of the veggie mix stayed in when flipping, but using the method of filling half of a tortilla and then flipping it also works well. Served with sour cream and hot sauce.
I work in a kitchen that mostly cooks meat dishes and this would be a great veggie option,I'm running it tomorrow 😋
I followed the instructions exactly as written. It was not only easy, but delicious!! I will definitely make this again.
Serve hot, as the leftovers get soggy. Serve with dipping options, such as salsa, guacamole, or sour cream. Very good!
I gave this 4 stars for the idea. I made it with the vegetables I had on hand. It was delicious.
Absolutely wonderful and super easy. Great for a quick bite.
Very good recipe. The sauteed vegetables counterbalance the cheese for a somewhat lighter meal. Delicious.

I really loved this quesadilla that I've made last summer too. I've brought all the veggies you would find at a farmer's market and purchased it at my local grocery store instead. I've made it with sour cream and homemade guacamole to give it some zip. No substitutes for this one. Love it!
I made this recipe minus the mushrooms, personal preference, very good! It was a nice surprise for my vegetarian daughter in law. She loved it!
